paragraphs.text: Polycystic kidney disease-2 (PKD2) is a form of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) caused by mutation in the PKD2 gene on chromosome 4. Koptides et al. (1999) stated that PKD2 accounts for approximately 15% of ADPKD cases, compared with approximately 85% for PKD1 on chromosome 16. Deltas (2001) noted that PKD1 and PKD2 disease could not be told apart on clinical grounds, but that patients with PKD2 mutations had a milder course, with an average age of onset 10 to 20 years later and a lower likelihood of reaching end-stage renal failure. Hateboer et al. (1999) concluded that, although clinically milder than PKD1, PKD2 has a deleterious impact on life expectancy and cannot be regarded as benign.
